Previously status was implemented as a tag,
which made it indistinguishable from actual tags,
and also the status could take on any string value.

Let's implement it as an Enum,
so that we can decide what values it can take,

commitResults.messageTitle: Status: add error message for invalid values

commitResults.messageBody:
ParseStatus currently parses status strings into tags.

Let's update it to parse status strings into Status objects.

StatusCommandParser calls parseStatus, which parses the input String
into a Tag.
This is now broken because parseStatus now parses input into a Status.

Let's temporarily fix this by making the parser call parseTag,
which has identical functionality to the previous parseStatus method.
59 status field

parseStatus currently replaces internal whitespaces with underscores.
Although this makes it slightly more user-friendly
(typing out all the underscores in status is a hassle),
it might cause more confusion about what is a valid Status input.

Let's make things more straightforward by requiring a valid status
to exactly match current Status values, including underscores.

commitResults.messageTitle: Index: enable hashing based on index value
commitResults.messageBody:
Index uses the default java hashing method,
which returns different hash values even for Index objects
with the same value.

This means that for HashSets of Indexes, multiple indexes
of the same value can exist.

Let's fix this by overriding the hashing method
and make hashing to be based on the value stored in Index.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Note class for candidate notes
commitResults.messageBody:
Recruiters need to keep recruitment and interview information with
each candidate, but Person has no field for free-form text.

Let's add a Note value class for later commits to attach to Person.
Unlike Address, Note accepts any text, including an empty string, so
notes stay optional and recruiters are not blocked by format rules
on what is meant to be free-form information.

Recruiters need notes on each candidate, and Note exists but is not
yet part of Person.

Let's add a note field to Person and pass a note at every place that
creates one. EditCommand carries the existing note over, so editing
another field does not wipe it. AddCommandParser, JsonAdaptedPerson
and SampleDataUtil pass an empty note until later commits let users
enter, save and see notes.

Notes are left out of isSamePerson, as two records with the same name
are the same candidate regardless of their notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save candidate notes to the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
Notes are part of Person, but JsonAdaptedPerson does not save them,
so any note would be lost when the app restarts.

Let's add a note field to JsonAdaptedPerson so notes are written to
and read from the data file. A missing note loads as an empty note
rather than an error, so data files saved before notes existed still
load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show candidate notes in the UI and messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Notes are saved with each candidate but are not shown anywhere, so
users cannot read the notes they record.

Let's show the note on the candidate card, below the email, and
include it in the message shown after add, delete and edit. The note
wraps so long notes stay readable, and is hidden when empty so cards
without notes look the same as before. Give some sample candidates
notes so new users can see what notes are for.

The card's grid column prefers a width of 150px, and JavaFX uses that
width to work out the card's height. A wrapped note then reserves
room for more lines than it needs, leaving an empty gap at the bottom
of the card. Drop that preferred width and keep each list cell as
wide as the list. As a side effect, cards with many tags also lose
the same empty gap.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add nt/ prefix for notes in add command
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates can have notes, but the add command has no way to set one,
so every candidate added through the app ends up with an empty note.

Let's accept an optional nt/NOTE in the add command, so a recruiter
can record details such as an interview date when adding a candidate.
As with the other single-valued fields, a repeated nt/ is rejected.

A note cannot contain a space followed by a prefix such as t/ or n/,
as the tokenizer starts a new field there. Supporting that would need
an escape syntax, which is more than the MVP needs, so tests pin down
the behaviour instead to make any later change to it deliberate.

Editing notes and documenting nt/ in the User Guide are left to
separate changes.

Person#hashCode includes the note, but no test calls it, so a
change that drops the note from the hash goes unnoticed. Java
collections such as HashSet rely on equal persons having equal hash
codes, so hashCode must stay consistent with equals, which already
compares notes.

Let's check that equal persons share a hash code and that persons
differing only in their note get different hash codes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove nt/ prefix from add command
commitResults.messageBody:
The add command accepts an optional nt/NOTE, but the tokenizer ends
the note at the next recognized prefix. "nt/Discuss t/java" is saved
as the note "Discuss" plus a java tag, and "nt/Referee: n/Alice" is
rejected as a duplicate name, so valid notes are silently changed or
refused.

Notes are meant to be recorded on an existing candidate, usually
after an interview (UC06), which the add command cannot do anyway.

Let's remove nt/ from the add command, so new candidates start with
an empty note. A separate note command will set notes instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add note command to record candidate notes
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates can have notes, but there is no command to set or change
a note once the candidate has been added.

Let's add `note INDEX NOTE`, which replaces the note of the candidate
at INDEX, or clears it when NOTE is empty.

Taking everything after the index as the note lets a note hold any
text, so it avoids the misparsed notes that nt/ in the add command
produced. The User Guide documents the new command.

Some note command behaviour from issue #42 is untested or tested only
indirectly:

* The AddressBookParser test uses a plain note, so prefix-like text
  such as "t/" is checked only by NoteCommandParser, not after
  AddressBookParser splits off the command word.
* The "Call back" case in the invalid index test repeats the
  non-numeric index case, so it adds no coverage.
* Clearing the note of a person who has no note is untested.

Let's,
* use a note containing "t/" and "n/" in the AddressBookParser test
* replace the repeated case with "1Call back", a note joined to the
  index without a space
* check that clearing an empty note leaves the person unchanged and
  reports the note as cleared
Add notes to candidates

commitResults.messageTitle: Reword command messages from person to candidate
commitResults.messageBody:
Command messages shown to the recruiter use AB3 wording such as
"person" and "address book". RecruiterBuddy tracks candidates, so
this wording does not match what the recruiter sees elsewhere in the
product.

Let's replace "person" with "candidate" and "address book" with
"RecruiterBuddy" in the usage, success and error messages of the add,
edit, delete, list, find, note, clear and exit commands, and in the
shared messages in Messages.

Only the message text changes. Constant names stay the same because
open pull requests refer to them, and renaming them would break the
build once those are merged. Class names and the data file are left
for a separate rename. No test needs updating, as the tests refer to
the constants instead of repeating the text.
Reword command messages from person to candidate

A candidate's recruitment status is stored as a tag, so it cannot be
told apart from a free-form tag and a candidate can hold several.

Let's give Person a dedicated Status field. New candidates start as
PENDING_RESUME_SCREENING, and the edit, note and status commands
carry the existing status over when they rebuild a candidate.

The Person constructor takes the status explicitly rather than
defaulting it, so that a caller cannot reset a status by omission.

The status is not saved yet and the status command still adds a
tag; these follow separately.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save candidate status in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A candidate's status is lost when the app closes, because
JsonAdaptedPerson does not store it.

Let's save the status under its enum name and read it back on
startup.

A missing status loads as the default, so that data files saved
before this field existed still load. An unrecognized status is
rejected like any other invalid field, and must match the enum name
exactly, as role status does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show candidate status on the candidate card
commitResults.messageBody:
A candidate's status is stored but not visible in the GUI.

Let's show it first in the tag row, in a different color, so that it
stands apart from the candidate's free-form tags.

No test builds the sample data, so a duplicate or invalid sample
candidate would only surface when a first-time user launches the
app.

Let's check that the sample address book builds with every sample
candidate, and that each one starts with the default status.
Add a status field to candidates

Candidates have no record of which role opening they are applying
for, so a recruiter cannot tell which candidates belong to which
role.

Let's give every candidate a required role title:

* add requires r/ROLE and saves the title with the candidate
* edit, note and status keep the candidate's existing role
* edit rejects r/, so it is not silently read as part of another
  field's value, until changing a role is supported
* a saved candidate with a missing or invalid role is invalid data

A missing role is rejected rather than defaulted, as there is no role
every candidate could sensibly fall back to. Data files saved before
this change therefore fail to load.

Checking that the role exists and is open is left to a later commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject candidates for missing or closed roles
commitResults.messageBody:
A candidate's role title is checked only for its format, so a
candidate can be added to a role that does not exist or whose hiring
has finished.

Let's check the role against the roles in RecruiterBuddy:

* add rejects a role that does not exist or is closed
* add saves the role's own spelling of the title, so r/software
  engineer is saved as Software Engineer
* loading rejects a saved candidate whose role is not in the roles
  list, but accepts one whose role is closed, as closing a role keeps
  its candidates

Roles are matched ignoring case, as role titles are already unique
ignoring case.

The sample data gains the roles of the sample candidates, so that it
satisfies the same rule.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show candidate role on candidate card
commitResults.messageBody:
The role a candidate is applying for is saved but not shown, so a
recruiter cannot see which role each candidate belongs to.

Let's show the role on its own line below the candidate's name. It
stays out of the tag row, which holds the status and tags, so that it
is not mistaken for either.
Add candidates to an open role

The User Guide does not describe the candidate features added for

address book.

Let's update the candidate parts of the guide to match the app:

* add: document the required r/ROLE, that the role must exist and be

* edit: note that the role cannot be changed and that status and note
  are kept
* note: show recording an interview date and time
* Reword the candidate command sections to candidate and RecruiterBuddy
* Fix the Quick start and command summary add examples, and note that
  clear also deletes roles

Role rules are left to the role add section rather than repeated here.
The data file sections are updated separately in #76.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update Developer Guide for candidate roles and notes
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide does not cover the candidate features added for
v1.3. UC02, UC04 and UC06 render as single paragraphs, the use case
intro names AddressBook as the system, there is no implementation
section for notes, and the manual tests still refer to persons.

Let's bring the candidate parts of the guide up to date:

* Lay out UC02, UC04 and UC06 like UC01 in #76, and name RecruiterBuddy
  and the recruiter in the use case intro
* UC02: add extensions for invalid details, a missing role and a
  closed role
* UC04: ask for the interview date and time, with extensions for
  invalid input, interviewers and rescheduling
* UC06: add extensions for a missing candidate, removing notes and an
  empty note
* Add a Candidate notes implementation section, recording why the
  nt/ prefix was dropped in favour of a separate note command
* Add manual tests for adding and editing candidates and recording
  notes, and reword the delete tests to refer to candidates

The use cases describe the full product rather than v1.3, so some
behaviour, such as the duplicate warning in UC02 and the separate
interview record in UC04, is not implemented yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Replace remaining AB3 references
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide title and intro still describe AddressBook Level 3, the
Quick start downloads the JAR from se-edu's releases, and the Quick

Let's rename the guide to RecruiterBuddy, describe the product in the

The role and data file sections are left alone, as #74 and #76 update

Keep master's new sections as written and use the renamed headings,
as the two changes do not overlap in content.

The Help window links to the AB3 user guide on se-education.org,

commitResults.messageTitle: MainWindow: Rename window title to RecruiterBuddy

The main window title reads "Address App", left over from the

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore candidate wording in command messages

The list success message, the listed-count message and the invalid

Master adds UC01 extensions and restructures UC07 into the formatted

Keep both sets of changes so the guide reflects the latest role

Update User and Developer Guides for candidate features

Several pages still describe AddressBook-Level3 rather than
RecruiterBuddy. The User Guide refers to the address book and to
persons, the Developer Guide keeps AB3's sample "Delete a person" use

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Align duplicate and interview claims with v1.3
commitResults.messageBody:
The README promises duplicate detection by phone number or email and
structured interview tracking, and the matching user stories are
marked must-have. v1.3 detects duplicates by exact name only and
records interviews as free-text notes, so the docs overstate the MVP.

Let's describe the delivered behaviour and defer the rest:

* README and User Guide state the name-based duplicate rule and that
  interview dates are recorded as notes without validation.
* Split the duplicate and interview user stories so the must-have
  stories match what v1.3 delivers, and move phone/email warnings,
  date/time checking and interview filtering to lower priorities.
* Reword the status story, as `status` replaces the existing status
  in one step rather than removing it first.

Use cases are left unchanged, as they describe the full product
rather than the MVP.

commitResults.messageTitle: README, index.md: Describe delivered MVP features
commitResults.messageBody:
The feature lists in the README and the website home page call the
features "planned" and leave out delivered behaviour. They omit
editing, finding and deleting candidates, deleting roles, the
one-hire-per-role rule and the role closure conditions. The home page
also keeps the old duplicate and interview claims, and the help
bullet implies an in-app guide rather than a link to the User Guide.

Let's present the list as the delivered MVP and describe each
feature as v1.3 implements it, keeping both pages identical so
the README and website agree.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Correct command details that do not match the app
commitResults.messageBody:
Several User Guide details contradict how commands behave. The
command summary's `status 1 accepted` example fails, as ACCEPTED is
not a status. The command-format notes say extra parameters to `list`
are ignored, but `list` accepts only `list` or `list role`. The note
section says notes are saved exactly as typed, but surrounding spaces
are trimmed.

Let's use HIRED in the status example, limit the extra-parameter rule
to `help`, `exit` and `clear` while stating what `list` accepts, and
mention that the note is trimmed.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Fix UC06 and UC08 to match note and delete
commitResults.messageBody:
UC06 says an empty note is rejected, but entering a note command
without text clears the note, which extension 1b already covers.
UC08 lets the user select multiple records for deletion, but delete
removes one candidate selected by index. UC08 also uses a plain-text
layout that renders as one paragraph, unlike the other use cases.

Let's remove UC06's empty-note extension and rewrite UC08 as a
single-candidate deletion in the same format as UC02 to UC07.

commitResults.messageTitle: SettingUp: Require JDK 25 instead of JDK 17
commitResults.messageBody:
The setup guide tells developers to configure IntelliJ with JDK 17,
but the build requires Java 25, so following the guide leads to a
failed build.

Let's ask for JDK 25 to match the build and the documented NFRs.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Renumber use cases and drop stray scope note
commitResults.messageBody:
The MVP use cases are numbered UC01 to UC07, UC07a and UC08, with no
UC09 before the optional use cases begin at UC10. A lone "MVP scope"
note about role vacancies also sits after the candidate deletion use
case, where it reads as part of that use case even though UC01 and
the implementation section already state the one-vacancy rule.

Let's renumber UC07a and UC08 to UC08 and UC09 so the numbering runs
without gaps, and remove the redundant note.

UC03, UC05 and the optional use cases UC10 to UC25 are written as
plain lines, which the website merges into a single paragraph per use
case. The other MVP use cases already use headings and bold labels,
so the section looks inconsistent and the plain ones are hard to read.

Let's give every use case a heading, bold System, Actor, main success
scenario and Extensions labels, and bulleted extensions. The wording
of each use case is unchanged.

The startup log reports the app version as V0.5.1, a value carried
over from AB3. Logs from the v1.3 release would then show the wrong
version, which can mislead anyone diagnosing a reported problem.

Let's set VERSION to V1.3 to match the upcoming release.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Require launching from the JAR folder
commitResults.messageBody:
RecruiterBuddy resolves its data, preferences and log file paths
against the working directory. Launching it from another folder, such
as by double-clicking the JAR on some systems, makes it read and write
those files outside the JAR's folder. This breaks the course's
Constraint-Data-Sandbox. The DG manual tests also tell testers to
double-click the JAR, which can make them misreport saving as broken.

Let's document the required launch method until the paths are fixed
in code:

* Quick Start: warn to always launch from a terminal in the JAR's
  folder
* Data file section: state that the file is saved relative to the
  launch folder and created after the first successful command
* FAQ: replace the AB3 "home folder" wording
* Known issues: describe the wrong-folder symptom and a recovery that
  backs up both data files before choosing one
* DG launch tests: run the JAR from a terminal instead of
  double-clicking, and expect only preferences.json and addressbook.log
  on first launch

This is a workaround, not full compliance, since the app can still
access files elsewhere if launched differently.

Configuration.md describes a config.json file that controls the log
level and the preferences file location. AB3 removed that support,
so the app ignores config.json, and no page links to the guide. The
site map's "Documentation, logging, testing, configuration, dev-ops"
link also points to an anchor that does not exist, as the DG heading
has no "configuration".

Let's delete the guide and point the site map link to the DG's
"Documentation, logging, testing, dev-ops" heading. The Logging guide
already explains how to change the log level.
Align docs with v1.3 behaviour before release

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Interview class for interview dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates have no way to record an interview slot, so recruiters
type it into the note, where a mistyped or impossible date goes
unnoticed.

Let's add an Interview value class that accepts only zero-padded
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM values that are real dates and 24-hour times, and
an Interview.NONE value for candidates with no interview.

Format errors and impossible values get separate messages, as PE
testers treat calling an invalid value a format error as a bug.
ParserUtil.parseInterview exposes both checks for the upcoming
interview command and for loading saved data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Person: Add interview field and save it to storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates need an interview date and time that the card, storage
and the upcoming interview command can rely on.

Let's add an Interview field to Person, defaulting to Interview.NONE,
and save it in the data file. A missing or empty interview loads as
no interview, so files saved by v1.3 still load.

Every command that rebuilds a Person (note, status, edit, and role
changes) now copies the interview, so updating another field never
wipes it. The sample data moves Alex Yeoh's interview out of the note
into the new field, and mixes candidates with and without interviews
so both card states are visible.

Saved interviews are not visible anywhere, so recruiters cannot see
when a candidate's interview is.

Let's show the interview on the candidate card as
"Interview: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", in the same form users type it, and
hide the line for candidates with no interview so their cards have no
blank row. Command results that list a candidate's details now
include the interview as well.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add interview command to schedule interviews
commitResults.messageBody:
Recruiters can see a candidate's interview but have no command to
set it.

Let's add "interview INDEX d/YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" to schedule or replace
an interview, and "interview INDEX" to clear it. Results name the
updated candidate, so recruiters can tell who changed when working
through a filtered list.

An empty d/ is rejected instead of clearing the interview, so a
mistyped date never wipes an existing one. Clearing a candidate with
no interview, or repeating the same date, still succeeds, as with
note. The command keeps the current filter, which the planned
find-and-update workflow relies on.

The guide tells users to type interview dates into notes, where
nothing checks them, and does not mention the interview command.

Let's add an interview section with the date rules, how to clear an
interview, and examples, worded to match the error messages. Point
note users to interview for dates, describe the interview field in
the data file section, and add the command to the summary table.

The guide describes notes as the place for interview dates, has no
section on how interviews are implemented, and UC04 promises
interviewer and location details that the product does not record.

Let's add a "Candidate interviews" implementation section covering
validation, the command, storage, and the main design decisions.
Update UC04 to match the command, including clearing and the two
kinds of invalid date, and replace the interview-style note examples
in manual testing. Add manual tests for scheduling, rejecting
invalid dates, keeping the filter, and saving interviews.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: State what interview does when nothing changes
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide says clearing an empty interview or repeating the same date
"changes nothing", which a reader could take to mean the command is
ignored or shows a different message.

State instead that such commands still succeed with the usual result
message and leave the candidate unchanged, so the guide describes
exactly what users will see.

commitResults.messageTitle: NoteCommand: Name the candidate in the result message
commitResults.messageBody:
The note result message prints every field of the updated candidate.
The result box shows only the start of that line, so a recruiter
working through a filtered list cannot easily tell whose note changed
or what was saved.

Let's shorten the message to the candidate's name and the new note,
or the name alone when the note is cleared, so the important part
fits in the result box.

Also add an assertion that the edited candidate holds the new note,
and log each note change to help trace issues.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update name and phone validation rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Names allow only ASCII letters, digits and spaces, so real names such
as O'Brien, Tan, Mei Ling or Ravi s/o Kumar are rejected. Phones accept
any 3 or more digits, so numbers that cannot be real are accepted.

Let's make names 1 to 100 characters long, starting with a letter in
any language, and allow digits, spaces and ' - . , / ( ) after it.
Accent marks are allowed too, as an accented letter can be typed as a
plain letter followed by a separate mark.

Let's make phones 8 to 15 digits with an optional leading +, allowing
single spaces or hyphens between digits. Phone stores the number
without separators, so differently formatted inputs of the same number
are equal and the data file holds one canonical form.

Update the User Guide with both rules and a tip to write a/l and a/p
as A/L and A/P, since a/ starts the address. Pad the 7-digit phones in
the test data so it satisfies the new phone rule.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore phone separators and clarify UG field rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Phones accept only single spaces or hyphens between digits, so common
inputs such as 9123 - 4567 or + 65 9123 4567 are rejected even though
their digits are valid. The UG states the name and phone rules as long
sentences placed between the ROLE notes, which makes them hard to find
and scan.

Let's ignore all spaces and hyphens in phones and check only for an
optional leading + and 8 to 15 digits. The digit count and the +
position are what make a number valid; the separators carry no
meaning, and they are removed when saved anyway.

Let's also list the name and phone rules as short bullets in parameter
order, describing what is accepted rather than giving orders, and word
the error messages the same way. Use PHONE_NUMBER consistently in the
edit command format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add defensive checks to Name and Phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Name.isValidName and Phone.isValidPhone reject a null argument only
indirectly, through the NullPointerException of the first method call
on it. The Phone constructor assumes that removing separators from a
valid phone always leaves an optional + followed by digits, but
nothing checks this.

Let's state the non-null contract with requireNonNull, so a null
fails fast at the method boundary, and assert the stored phone's form
so that a future change to separator removal that breaks it is caught
during development.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect duplicate candidates by email or phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates are treated as duplicates when their names match. This
blocks different people who share a name, while letting the same
person be added twice under another spelling of their name.

Let's treat two candidates as duplicates when their emails match,
ignoring case, or their phone numbers match. Names may now repeat.
Phone numbers are compared as saved, so a number with and without
its country code count as different; the User Guide documents this.

add and edit name the existing candidate and the clashing field.
edit excludes the candidate being edited, so keeping their own email
does not hide a clash with another candidate's phone number. The
same rule applies when loading the data file.

# Conflicts:
#	docs/UserGuide.md
#	src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/commands/EditCommand.java
Name the updated candidate in the note result message

# Conflicts:
#	docs/UserGuide.md

commitResults.messageTitle: Phone: Remove redundant assert on stored value
commitResults.messageBody:
The Phone constructor asserts that the stored value matches
VALIDATION_REGEX right after checkArgument has validated the same
separator-stripped string against the same regex. The assert can
never fail, and its unreachable failure branch leaves the line
partially covered, dropping patch coverage below the Codecov target.

Let's remove the assert. The constructor still rejects invalid input
through checkArgument, so the stored value is guaranteed to be valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Log rejected duplicates and clarify duplicate messages
commitResults.messageBody:
A rejected duplicate add or edit leaves no trace in the log beyond
the command text, so the reason for the rejection is lost. The data
file error says only "duplicate person(s)", which does not say what
makes two candidates duplicates.

Let's log each rejected add or edit with the clashing candidate and
field, as #87 asks. The data file error now names the email and
phone rule, and the duplicate message helper rejects null arguments
before its assertion runs.

The User Guide example now uses +6591234567, which needs the phone
format from #82, so this branch should be merged after #82.

master adds editing a candidate's role, renaming roles and backing up
unreadable data files. Both sides changed EditCommand and the User
Guide's edit and data file sections.

Keep master's role-edit messages and drop its generic duplicate
message, which the email and phone messages replace. Add the
duplicate rule to master's new edit and data file text.

master's new tests build candidates that differ only by name, which
now clash by email or phone. Give them distinct contact details, and
check a clashing email instead of a shared name during a transfer.

Master and this branch both change NoteCommand: master adds an assert
and names the candidate in the success message, while this branch
passes the new interview field through when rebuilding the Person.

Keep both changes in NoteCommand, and update the interview-preserving
NoteCommandTest case to expect master's new message format so it no
longer fails with a missing format argument.
Update name and phone validation

Master adds name and phone validation rules (#112), including a User
Guide bullet on candidate fields in the data file. This branch adds a
bullet on duplicate emails and phones to the same list, so the two
edits conflict.

Keep both bullets in a single list, with master's name and phone rules
first, so the data-file section documents every constraint the loader
enforces.
Detect duplicate candidates by email or phone
Add interview command to schedule candidate interviews

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Add candidate and interview diagrams
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG describes a candidate's fields and the interview command only
in text. The model class diagram omits candidate fields, so readers
cannot see how a candidate holds its role, note, status and interview,
or how interview INDEX clears an interview.

Let's add a candidate class diagram showing each field with its
implemented multiplicity, and an interview sequence diagram covering
parsing, date and time validation, the displayed-candidate lookup, the
model update and saving. Interview and Status use plain associations,
as Interview.NONE and the status constants are shared by candidates.

The DG text now states that scheduling another interview replaces the
previous one.

The interview sequence diagram draws the argument tokenizer, the
argument multimap and the role-list guard as separate calls. These
are shared by every command or matter only when they fail, so they
lengthen the diagram without explaining the interview feature.

Let's describe them in notes instead, keeping the calls for parsing,
date and time validation, lookup, replacement, model update and
saving.

The candidate class diagram also shows member visibility as
PlantUML icons, which readers may not recognise. Show the UML
symbols + and - instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix build broken by merging #122 and #123
commitResults.messageBody:
Each PR passes CI on its own, but master fails after both are merged.
Both add a logger field to EditCommand, so EditCommand declares
logger twice and does not compile. A new diagnostics test from #122
also adds a candidate that differs from another only by name, which
#123's email-or-phone rule treats as a duplicate.

Let's remove the second logger declaration, and give the test's
second candidate its own email and phone, as other tests already do
since #123.
Fix build broken by merging #122 and #123
Add UML diagrams for candidate structure and interviews

The project landing pages still describe the original AddressBook

and planned MVP scope. This ensures that the pages reflect the

The Developer Guide still targets users managing generic contacts.

Define the department recruiter target profile and value proposition
so that the requirements match RecruiterBuddy's product direction.

The existing user stories describe generic contact management and do
not capture the recruitment workflow.

Replace them with prioritised RecruiterBuddy stories covering the MVP
and optional future requirements.
21 AboutUs: Update Kavin's details
Corrected the naming of Samuel's image file within the img source.
Update product documentation

RecruiterBuddy has no shared representation for role openings, which
prevents role features from storing or observing role data.

Introduce validated immutable roles, unique role storage, JSON
persistence, and observable model and logic access. This provides a
stable foundation for adding and listing roles.

commitResults.messageTitle: Derive role limits in constraint messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Role validation messages repeat their length bounds as literals, which can
leave user guidance inconsistent when a bound changes.

Define the bounds as constants and build each message from them. This keeps
validation and guidance tied to one source of truth.
Add persistent role model

Persistent roles exist but recruiters cannot record new vacancies
through the command interface.

Add the role add command with validation and duplicate protection.
Create each accepted role as an open vacancy and expose it through the
observable role list.

The role parser duplicates existing prefix validation while producing
a less specific error message.

Reuse ArgumentMultimap's field-specific duplicate check and remove the
local helper so role commands follow established parser behavior.

The shared role command word is owned by AddRoleCommand, making future
role subcommands depend on an add-specific class.

Move the command word and group usage to RoleCommandParser. Show the
available role add syntax when a bare role command is entered.
Add role opening command
Revert "Updated commands and user guide."

Recruiters need to finish recruitment while preserving role and
candidate records.

Add explicit role closure after checking all associated candidates
have final outcomes and at most one is hired. Retain candidate data
and prevent new applications to the closed role.

Mistaken role openings need to be removed without losing candidate
records.

Allow deletion only when no candidates are associated with the role.
Release its title for reuse and persist the updated role list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Prevent multiple hires for one role
commitResults.messageBody:
Each role represents one vacancy, but status updates currently allow
multiple candidates for the same role to be hired.

Reject assigning HIRED when another associated candidate is already
hired. Check all stored candidates and preserve data on rejection.

Role index guards can use stale view state after a successful command
switches the UI back to candidates. This permits closing or deleting
a hidden role.

Record the displayed list centrally from the successful command result.
Preserve candidate filters when listing roles and leave view state
unchanged when execution or saving fails.

commitResults.messageTitle: Prevent pending statuses for closed roles
commitResults.messageBody:
Closed recruitment can currently regain pending candidates through
status updates.

Reject pending statuses for candidates whose role is closed. Keep
corrections available for open roles and preserve records on rejection.
Add role close and delete commands

Role creation and storage are implemented, but their constraints
and design are not fully explained.

Document role validation, identity, persistence, and recovery.
Update the model and storage diagrams to match the implementation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify role lifecycle and testing guidance
commitResults.messageBody:
Role lifecycle details are mixed into use cases, and the
requirements still imply support for multiple openings.

Separate implementation guidance from use cases and document
manual checks for role lifecycle rules and persistence.
Document role management and persistence

Failed recruitment-data loading currently opens an editable empty
session. A later successful command saves that empty state and can
overwrite the original records, leaving users without their data.

Stop startup with a visible error identifying the affected file.
Prevent command execution after a load failure and preserve existing
behaviour for valid files and genuinely missing files.

Failing closed protects the original without treating unreadable
data as an intentionally empty recruitment database. Keep automatic
backup and recovery for a later increment so this first change
provides independently useful protection with a smaller failure
surface.

Route null JSON data and null records through loading errors so those
inputs receive the same protection instead of failing outside it.

Add regression tests and update the loading documentation to explain
the failure behaviour and distinguish it from missing-file startup.

Candidate roles cannot currently be corrected through edit. Removing
and recreating a candidate to fix an association risks losing notes,
status and other recruitment details.

Support role changes through the existing edit command and preserve
all fields that the recruiter does not explicitly change. Resolve
the destination using the stored role's canonical title.

Allow corrections from closed source roles, but require an open
destination so reassignment cannot resume recruitment for a closed
vacancy. Preserve candidate status rather than silently resetting
their progress, and reject hired transfers that would fill a role
more than once.

Share the single-hire check with status updates so both workflows
enforce the same rule across all stored candidates. Permit selecting
the current role as a no-op so closed roles do not block unrelated
corrections.

Add parser, command and persistence regression tests, and document
the reassignment rules and updated-candidate success message.

Recruiters cannot currently correct a role's required experience
without removing and recreating the opening. Deletion is unavailable
once candidates belong to the role.

Add role edit with the existing experience-level validation and
displayed-role index safeguards. Preserve the role's title, status
and candidates so correcting its requirements does not alter hiring
history or reopen recruitment.

Replace the immutable role through the existing model API so the
observable list and persistence follow the established workflow.

Keep title changes separate because they also require updating
candidate associations. Add regression tests and document this
working experience-only increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show candidate status counts on role cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Role cards show vacancy details but do not summarise their candidates.
Recruiters must inspect individual records to understand each role's
recruitment progress.

Show pending, hired, rejected and withdrawn totals for every role.
Count all associated candidates so filtering the candidate list does
not hide part of the recruitment pipeline.

Derive totals from current records rather than persisting another
copy of the data. Observe candidate-list changes so status corrections,
removals and role transfers cannot leave the displayed totals stale.

Keep counting separate from JavaFX rendering so the classification
and association rules can be tested independently. Constrain card
width and wrap long details so indices and totals remain readable.
Add regression tests and document the role-card summaries.

commitResults.messageTitle: Recover safely from unreadable recruitment data
commitResults.messageBody:
Unreadable recruitment data currently prevents startup until users
repair or move the file themselves. A small editing mistake can
therefore block all recruitment work.

Back up the original file without replacing existing backups, then
start with empty candidate and role lists. Explain the backup location
and restoration steps in a visible startup warning.

Persist the empty replacement so restarting does not unexpectedly
load sample records. Continue only after the original is protected;
stop with recovery instructions if safe recovery cannot complete.

Add regression tests and update the guides and startup diagram to
describe both successful recovery and failure handling.

Role edits use inconsistent error wording and repeat the role-change
comparison in separate validation paths.

Align the messages with add while keeping edit-specific recovery
instructions. Extract a shared role-change predicate so destination
and hiring checks use the same identity rule.

Preserve existing transfer restrictions and same-role corrections.
Update documentation and regression tests to match.
Allow candidate role reassignment

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject trailing content in saved JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
JSON loading accepts the first root value and ignores additional
content. A later save can silently discard that content.

Require parsing to consume the complete input so invalid files enter
the existing backup-and-recovery flow. Preserve the entire original
file rather than attempting an ambiguous partial import.

Use the shared parsing boundary without upgrading dependencies or
changing valid-file behaviour. Add regression tests and document the
single-root requirement and existing preference-error fallback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge latest master into data recovery branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master includes candidate role reassignment and enabled assertions.
Its contribution acknowledgement overlaps the startup-recovery entry,
preventing this branch from merging cleanly into the team repository.

Merge master and combine the acknowledgement to retain both scopes.
Preserve the existing feature commits and master changes rather than
rewriting published history or dropping either contribution.

Verify the combined product with the full tests, coverage, coding
checks, documentation build and packaged-JAR recovery smoke checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove hard wrapping from role edit paragraph
commitResults.messageBody:
The role-edit parser explanation is split at a fixed line length,
contrary to the SE-EDU Markdown guideline for prose.

Keep the paragraph on one source line without changing its wording.
This allows editor soft wrapping to handle readability without
reflowing adjacent source lines whenever the text is edited.
Allow editing role experience levels

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename roles and update candidate associations
commitResults.messageBody:
Role editing supports experience corrections but not title changes.
Candidates store role titles, so changing only the role would leave
their associations inconsistent.

Extend role edit with optional title and experience fields. Validate
the complete edit before updating the role and all its candidates.

Keep the cascade in the model and reuse immutable candidate copying
so hidden candidates are updated without losing recruitment history.
Preserve the existing storage format and add regression coverage
and matching documentation.
Protect unreadable recruitment data

commitResults.messageTitle: Add diagnostics to role management workflows
commitResults.messageBody:
Role operations enforce recruitment rules, but their diagnostic
coverage is uneven when investigating rejected changes or broken
candidate associations.

Record operation outcomes and assert internal status and role
lookup contracts before candidate mutations.

Keep user validation exception-based and reuse LogsCenter so
diagnostics do not change command behavior or introduce another
logging system. Omit candidate details from the new records and
distinguish in-memory changes from persistence.

Recovery already records backup and replacement completion, but
regression tests do not verify those diagnostic events.

Test successful recovery and failure diagnostics, including paths
chosen after collisions and the absence of false success records.
Share in-memory log capture with role workflow tests and verify
that it restores logging configuration even when a test fails.

Document event levels and privacy limitations while retaining
the existing recovery policy and production logging.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain role editing with a sequence diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The current sequence hides validation and candidate propagation in notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify undo support for role changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Role guidance describes deletion as permanent and reopening as
unsupported even though undo restores earlier role snapshots.
These statements hide an existing recovery option from recruiters.

Clarify session-scoped undo and redo for deletion and closure,
and distinguish undo from a dedicated reopen command.

Keep undo behavior unchanged and add regression tests so the
corrected guidance matches the saved application state.

Repair the guide markup so these instructions render in the
published site rather than appearing as raw Markdown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept common punctuation in role titles
commitResults.messageBody:
Role titles reject punctuation used in ordinary job names such as
C++ Developer, C# Developer and Engineer (Backend). Recruiters must
alter those names before recording their vacancies.

Allow plus signs, hashes, parentheses and commas in RoleTitle.
Update the guides and test creation, candidate association,
renaming and persistence with these titles.

Keep validation in the shared value object so commands and saved
data accept the same titles without duplicating validation rules.
Preserve existing length, letter and duplicate constraints.

commitResults.messageBody:
Role-title errors mention only length and a required letter, so a

List the allowed characters on a second line of the shared error.
Update the guides and verify the complete message across role and
candidate commands, value construction and JSON validation.

Keep one constraint message for all entry points so correction
advice stays consistent without changing the accepted-title rules.
